incidents.victim: Afghanistan Ministry of Finance and provincial finance officials
incidents.vector: Phishing emails delivered ZIP archives with Pashto-language lures masquerading as internal seminar documents, hosted on a compromised Afghan education domain to blend with legitimate government traffic.
incidents.impact: XenoRAT remote access trojan silently installed on victim systems and connected to attacker-controlled servers in Europe, giving long-term spying capability against ministry and provincial revenue/finance staff.

incidents.victim: Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Attackers used a VPN address near the target's hometown, then tricked Meta's AI customer support assistant into linking a new email to the account during a password-reset flow and triggering a one-time code.
incidents.impact: High-profile U.S. government Instagram accounts briefly defaced with pro-Iran imagery and messages; hackers also claimed to have hijacked short, high-value Instagram handles allegedly worth more than $500,000. Meta issued an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.victim: Pay Tel (US inmate calling service)
incidents.vector: Cloud storage bucket left exposed on the public internet without a password for at least a week.
incidents.impact: 3.4 million scanned images exposed, including driver's licenses, legal documents and financial records belonging to inmates and their contacts.

incidents.victim: U.S.-based law firms (100+ targets, surge in 2026)
incidents.vector: Phishing emails or phone calls urge employees to call a fake IT support line; if remote-access attempts fail, the group physically dispatches operatives to victim offices to plug a storage device into a workstation and copy data.
incidents.impact: FBI re-issued a public alert after activity surged, noting more than 100 confirmed attacks since 2022. Halcyon tracked 134 ransomware incidents against the legal sector in Q1 2026, with Silent Ransom Group a top contributor. Data theft is leveraged for high-pressure extortion against firms holding sensitive client information.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (VS Code, npm, PyPI, 300+ GitHub repos)
incidents.vector: Malicious code seeded into VS Code extensions, npm/Python packages, and GitHub repositories with command-and-control split across Solana blockchain, BitTorrent, Google Calendar and rented VPS infrastructure for resilience.
incidents.impact: Windows, macOS and Linux systems infected with credential and data theft and the GlasswormRAT remote-access tool since early 2025. CrowdStrike, Google and Shadowserver coordinated a simultaneous takedown of four attacker-controlled servers, disrupting the operation.

incidents.victim: Wiley Rein LLP (260-attorney U.S. regulatory law firm)
incidents.vector: Phishing email used to compromise Microsoft 365 email accounts of select Wiley Rein personnel; the firm acknowledged no MFA or basic safeguards were in place.
incidents.impact: Attackers maintained undetected access from July 2024 through June 2025. Stolen data included names, addresses, dates of birth, financial accounts, medical information and Social Security numbers — including for third parties with no direct relationship to the firm. Class action filed May 26 alleges at least 19 fraudulent charges against the named plaintiff.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Intrusion details not publicly disclosed; Iran-linked group Ababil of Minab claimed responsibility and Israeli firm Gambit Security provided forensic evidence linking the operation to MOIS after attackers inadvertently exposed stolen data online.
incidents.impact: At least 700 GB of emails, backups and files stolen; LACMTA forced to shut down parts of its network in March. The same group is tied to attacks on Tri-Rail (South Florida), vehicle-tracker Vyncs, and Saudi infrastructure firm Unimac.

incidents.victim: KnowledgeDeliver LMS customer (Japan)
incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey shared across all KnowledgeDeliver deployments before Feb 24, 2026 to forge ViewState payloads for unauthenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-5426); deployed BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) in-memory web shell.
incidents.impact: Web servers compromised; attacker modified site JavaScript to push fake security-plugin prompts that delivered Cobalt Strike BEACON backdoors to website visitors, with payloads pre-encrypted using the targeted organization's name.

incidents.victim: Two unnamed Vietnamese government agencies
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; intrusions ran undetected before being uncovered.
incidents.impact: Compromised networks store the data of millions of Vietnamese citizens; the government opened formal investigations after the breaches were discovered.

incidents.victim: Northern Mariana Islands government
incidents.vector: Not publicly specified.
incidents.impact: Email servers for the US territory disrupted; officials warned of slowed administrative tasks while systems were recovered.

incidents.victim: MyPillow
incidents.vector: Initial access vector not publicly disclosed; Play affiliates typically rely on phishing or exploitation of internet-facing services.
incidents.impact: Play ransomware group claims theft of sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network and is extorting the company; MyPillow had not confirmed the incident at time of reporting.

incidents.victim: Lithuania state property registry
incidents.vector: Compromised credentials issued to other Lithuanian government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data were used to access and exfiltrate registry records.
incidents.impact: 600,000 records exfiltrated, including real names, cadastral information and other property details.

incidents.victim: Charter Communications
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters/Bling Libra's documented playbook of vishing for credentials and MFA codes, then registering attacker-controlled devices to maintain persistence in customer SaaS tenants.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a security breach after being publicly listed on the ShinyHunters dark web leak portal; scope of customer data exposed not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: Wahlap (Chinese arcade machine maker)
incidents.vector: Elasticsearch database left exposed on the public internet without authentication for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal details of nearly 19 million customers exposed — including phone numbers and full names tied to WeChat accounts. Data remained accessible until the server was eventually secured.

incidents.victim: GitHub (Microsoft) internal repositories
incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed a compromised Nx Console VS Code extension that had itself been poisoned via the upstream TanStack supply-chain attack; the extension exfiltrated repositories from the developer machine.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories exfiltrated and offered for sale on cybercrime forums. GitHub rotated critical secrets and isolated the affected endpoint; says no customer data outside the internal repos was affected. The same TanStack chain also led to a confirmed Grafana breach days earlier.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor employed by Nightwing created a public GitHub profile named 'Private-CISA' and committed plaintext credentials, having explicitly disabled GitHub's built-in protection against publishing sensitive secrets. The repository was originally created in November 2025.
incidents.impact: Plaintext AWS GovCloud keys and credentials for dozens of internal CISA systems exposed publicly for roughly six months. An RSA private key with full read/admin access to all CISA-IT GitHub repositories was still valid more than a week after CISA was notified. Lawmakers in both chambers demanded answers and CISA is still rotating affected secrets.

incidents.victim: 5,500+ GitHub open-source repositories (Megalodon campaign)
incidents.vector: More than 5,700 malicious commits pushed across over 5,500 repositories injected GitHub Actions workflows containing payloads to steal credentials, keys, tokens and other secrets at build time.
incidents.impact: Widespread harvesting of CI/CD secrets across affected open-source projects, demonstrating how a coordinated burst of commits can poison the Actions pipeline at scale before defenders can react.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries successor entities (the.hosting / WorkTitans / MIRhosting)
incidents.attacker: Russia — state-linked influence and cyberattack operations
incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime agency FIOD raided three businesses and two data centres after investigations tied operators to EU-sanctioned Stark Industries Solutions and to infrastructure used in DDoS attacks against Danish government bodies during November 2025 municipal elections.
incidents.impact: Two operators (aged 57 and 39) arrested for violating EU sanctions law; more than 800 servers, laptops and phones seized; customer data on the seized servers reported as lost and unrecoverable. Effective dismantling of Russia's primary Western-Europe-based proxy and DDoS-staging conduit.

incidents.victim: Multiple Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect VPN customers
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257) in GlobalProtect portal/gateway exploited by forging authentication-override cookies when the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS service and cookie encryption.
incidents.impact: Successful exploitation observed across multiple customer environments since May 17; a second attack wave on May 21 saw attackers assigned VPN addresses and reach internal network resources. CISA added CVE-2026-0257 to KEV on May 29; Rapid7 urged organizations to treat it as critical despite the 7.8 CVSS score.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (North American factories)
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Foxconn confirmed a cyberattack against its North American manufacturing operations; the incident highlights persistent ransomware and disruption risk to the electronics manufacturing sector. Detailed scope and downtime not publicly released.

incidents.victim: NYC Health + Hospitals (at least 1.8 million individuals)
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected; hackers stole medical records along with biometric information including fingerprints and palm prints. Biometric data is irreplaceable, creating long-term identity-theft and impersonation risk for victims.

incidents.victim: Technology-sector organizations in U.S., Israel, UAE and two other Middle Eastern entities
incidents.vector: Tailored fake-job-application archives ('Hiring Portal.zip') and impersonations of a global air carrier and a popular video-conferencing platform delivered six new RAT variants via DLL sideloading and a novel AppDomainManager hijack that disabled .NET application security at initialization.
incidents.impact: Coordinated waves of compromises against high-value IT and engineering staff aligned with the regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026. Per-target command-and-control domains hosted on Azure, with the latest variants able to exfiltrate files in chunks. Continuous deployment cadence indicates sustained intelligence collection against Western and Israeli defense and tech supply chains.
